supporting_observations.claim: During the alert window, WS-MFISCHER-01 made repeated connections to the internal proxy at 10.55.20.30:8080. The observed connections include several roughly five-minute-spaced examples, but these records do not identify the external destination or establish that the sessions were HTTPS.

The observed destination is the organization's explicit proxy, which is an expected network path in this environment; the available connection records alone do not distinguish approved application traffic from malicious traffic.

known_telemetry_limitations: Winsec and Sysmon collection for WS-MFISCHER-01 was unavailable from 13:30 to 14:15 UTC, so endpoint process-to-network attribution for the alerted period is missing.
Proxy collection was unavailable from 13:30 to 14:15 UTC, so the external HTTPS destinations, proxy actions, and user-agent or request details for the alerted period are unavailable.
Zeek connection records show connections to the internal proxy but do not, by themselves, identify the tunneled external destinations or the initiating application.
claims_not_established: Whether the periodic proxy connections were generated by the approved LedgerLink updater or another approved application.
Whether the connections reached an approved service or an unauthorized or malicious destination.
Which process initiated the observed connections and what data, if any, was sent beyond the proxy.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover or obtain proxy logs for 13:30–14:15 UTC, including CONNECT destinations, actions, user agents, and byte counts for WS-MFISCHER-01.
Obtain endpoint process and network telemetry for the same interval to attribute the proxy connections to an executable.
Verify whether LedgerLink and its updater were installed and active on WS-MFISCHER-01, and compare updater execution and destination details with the observed connection times.
Check DNS and TLS/SNI records for the external destinations associated with the proxy sessions.
unrelated_findings: Before the alert window, max.fischer accessed a Google Docs document through the proxy; Google file-sharing is not listed as approved. This is separate from the alerted-period activity. (T236-00106, T236-00107)

Before the alert window, max.fischer launched cmd.exe and WMIC to query running services, then ran an encoded PowerShell command that queries stopped services and created a temporary file. These events are outside the alerted activity and do not establish what generated the later proxy connections. (T236-00020, T236-00024, T236-00131, T236-00133)
